items.preview: HOA Turnover in Florida: What Happens to Community Signs — at turnover the entrance monument becomes the HOA's and builder signs come down: what F.S. 720.307 requires (90% + 3 months, 90 days to deliver) and what the sign handoff file should hold
items.seo_title: HOA Turnover in Florida: What Happens to Community Signs
items.meta_description: At Florida HOA turnover, entrance monuments pass to the HOA and builder signs come down. What F.S. 720.307 requires and what the sign file should hold.

faq.q: Who owns the entrance sign after HOA turnover in Florida?
faq.a: The homeowners' association. The entrance monument and other permanent signs sit on common property, and Florida Statute 720.307(4) requires the developer to deliver deeds to common property and the association's tangible property to the resident-controlled board within 90 days of turnover. The builder's marketing signs, such as Now Selling signs, flags and model home markers, stay with the builder.

faq.q: When does a Florida HOA turn over from the developer to residents?
faq.a: Under s. 720.307(1), residents elect a majority of the board at the earliest of several events. The most common is three months after 90 percent of the parcels in all phases have been conveyed to buyers other than the developer. Residents elect at least one director earlier, once 50 percent of parcels are conveyed.

faq.q: What sign records should an HOA ask the developer for at turnover?
faq.a: The statute requires warranties in effect and a list of the association's contractors. Boards should also ask for a sign inventory with photos, paint and material specs, lighting details, shop drawings, and the name of the fabricator, so that repairs can be matched later. Brand 9 Signs in Orange Park can inventory an undocumented monument for a Clay, St. Johns or Duval County HOA.

items.body_md:
# HOA Turnover in Florida: What Happens to Community Signs

**Short answer:** When a Florida developer hands control of a homeowners' association to residents, the permanent signs (the entrance monument, amenity signs and any lit features) become the association's to own and maintain, while the builder's marketing signs come down. Florida Statute 720.307 says the developer must deliver deeds to common property, the association's tangible property and all warranties in effect. In practice the sign records are often incomplete. A good handoff includes a sign inventory, finish specs, lighting details and who built each sign. The time to plan it is at the first rendering, not the last closing.

## When does HOA turnover happen in Florida?

Under [s. 720.307](https://m.flsenate.gov/Statutes/720.307), residents elect a majority of the board when the earliest of several events happens. The usual one is **three months after 90 percent of the parcels in all phases have been conveyed** to buyers other than the developer. Others include the developer abandoning its duty to finish the amenities, a Chapter 7 bankruptcy, or the developer losing title to foreclosure. Residents get their first board seat earlier, at 50 percent of parcels conveyed.

After turnover the developer has **no more than 90 days** to deliver the association's documents and property, at the developer's expense.

## Which community signs belong to the HOA, and which belong to the builder?

Most new subdivisions in Clay County, St. Johns County and Jacksonville have two layers of signage, and they end up in very different places.

### Builder-owned marketing signs

These are model home address markers, "Now Selling" and "Coming Soon" signs, feather flags, lot and directional riders, and sales center signs. They belong to the builder's sales operation. They come down or move to the next community when the last homes sell.

### Association-owned permanent signs

These are the entrance monument and its letters, secondary entrance or phase monuments, amenity center and pool signs, mailbox kiosk signs, and any lighting attached to them. They sit on common property, so they pass to the association with the deeds and tangible property listed in 720.307(4)(a) and (4)(k).

The trouble starts where the two layers overlap. If a "Homes from the $300s" panel was bolted to the face of the monument, someone has to remove it cleanly, patch the face and match the paint. If the builder's logo was cut into the stone, it can't come off at all.

## What should the HOA receive for its signs at turnover?

The statute requires "any and all warranties in effect" (4)(p) and a list of contractors working for the association (4)(m). It doesn't mention sign drawings, finish schedules or spare parts, and those are what a board needs five years later when a letter falls off. A complete sign handoff file should include:

- **A sign inventory**, with the location, photo, size and materials of every permanent sign.
- **Finish specs**, with paint manufacturer and color codes, stucco or stone type, and letter material and finish.
- **Lighting details**, with fixture type, timer or photocell settings, and which meter powers it.
- **Shop drawings or renderings** for each sign, so a cracked panel or missing letter can be remade to match.
- **Who built it**, with the fabricator's name and contact details, plus any warranty that is still running.
- **Spare parts**, if any were made (extra letters or a spare panel).

Boards in Middleburg and other fast-growing parts of Clay County inherit monuments that are often only a few years old. Without this file, a simple repair turns into guesswork about what the sign is made of.

## How builders can plan signage for a clean turnover

The cleanest handoffs are designed in from the start:

1. **Keep marketing off the monument.** Put pricing, "Now Selling" and builder branding on separate, removable panels or freestanding signs, never on the permanent face.
2. **Name the community, not the builder,** on anything the HOA will own.
3. **Pick finishes the HOA can maintain,** with documented colors and materials a local shop can match.
4. **Hand over the file at turnover,** together with a walk-through of every permanent sign.

## Who handles both sides of community signage in Northeast Florida?

Brand 9 Signs has built signage for Florida home builders since 1986, including model home packages, community entrance monuments and the marketing signs in between. It is Florida's Official Lennar Signage Partner and has worked for builders including Pulte, KB, Mattamy, Toll Brothers and Dream Finders. Design, fabrication and installation are handled by Brand 9's own crews from its shop at 1970 Solomon St in Orange Park. Because the same shop builds both the temporary and the permanent signs, it can plan the turnover when the signs are first designed. HOA boards that inherit an undocumented monument can also ask Brand 9 to inventory it and match repairs. Call (904) 272-3395 or email team@brand9signs.com.

items.meta_description: How NAS Jax, Mayport and Blount Island buy signs: SAM.gov and CAGE, the UFC 3-120-01 sign standard, and the $15K card and $350K quote limits.

items.body_md:
# How Military Bases in Jacksonville Buy Signage

**Short answer:** Signs on the federal installations around Jacksonville, such as NAS Jacksonville, Naval Station Mayport and Marine Corps Support Facility Blount Island, are bought through federal procurement rather than a phone call to a local sign shop. The sign company has to be registered in SAM.gov with an active CAGE code, and the sign usually has to follow the Department of Defense sign standard, **UFC 3-120-01**. Orders under the **$15,000 micro-purchase threshold** can be paid with a government purchase card. Orders above that go out for quotes under **simplified acquisition, up to $350,000**, and anything larger goes through a full solicitation. Brand 9 Signs in Orange Park is a registered U.S. government contractor (CAGE 0VVG2) and works for GPO and DLA on a regular basis.

## Who actually buys a sign on a military base?

The person who needs the sign is rarely the person who buys it. A squadron or tenant command may want a new building ID sign, but the money moves through one of these channels:

- **The unit's government purchase card (GPC)**, for small, single-vendor buys under the micro-purchase threshold.
- **The installation's public works or facilities office**, for planned projects. In Jacksonville this means NAVFAC Southeast, which has its headquarters at NAS Jacksonville.
- **The U.S. Government Publishing Office (GPO)**, which buys printed products for federal agencies through its print procurement program. That can include printed signs and graphics.
- **The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA)**, which handles supply buys across the services.

Camp Blanding Joint Training Center in Clay County is run by the Florida National Guard through the Florida Department of Military Affairs. Depending on where the money comes from, a sign there may be bought under state rules instead of federal ones, so ask the contracting contact which rules apply before you write a scope.

## The three dollar thresholds that decide how an order moves

On October 1, 2025, the Federal Acquisition Regulation raised its main thresholds for inflation. For signage, the tiers now work like this:

### Under $15,000: micro-purchase

A cardholder can buy directly from a registered vendor, usually after getting one reasonable quote. Most building ID signs, room ID packages and small regulatory sign runs fall in this tier.

### $15,000 to $350,000: simplified acquisition

The buyer asks for quotes and usually sets the work aside for small businesses. A clear message schedule and drawings that follow the standard make your quote easy to compare with the others.

### Above $350,000: full competition

Installation-wide wayfinding programs and entrance gate packages often land here, under formal FAR procedures.

## What UFC 3-120-01 changes about the sign itself

UFC 3-120-01, *Design: Sign Standards*, is the unified DoD criteria for exterior signs. The services wrote it together so that a building ID sign at Mayport follows the same system as one on a base overseas. It organizes signs into families, including installation entrance, building identification, directional and regulatory signs, and it sets the typography, color and layout for each. Many installations add a base exterior architecture plan or a facilities standard on top of the UFC.

In practice, a federal sign order is a "match the system" job, not a design contest. The value a sign shop adds is getting the message schedule exactly right, holding the specified colors and letter sizes, and building something that still looks right after years of Florida sun and salt air.

## What to have ready before you ask for a quote

A quote comes back fast and accurate when the request includes:

1. **The sign family and type** from UFC 3-120-01 (for example, building identification).
2. **A message schedule**: the exact text for every sign, building numbers included.
3. **A location list** with photos of any existing signs the new ones must match.
4. **The funding path**: purchase card, purchase request or GPO.
5. **Base access details**, because contractor installers need credentials or an escort, and that affects the schedule.

## Why a local registered sign company helps

A registered shop that already works inside these systems removes a step for the contracting office. Brand 9 Signs has built signs since 1986 and does design, renderings, fabrication in its Orange Park shop, and installation with its own crews and trucks. Its government work includes NAVFAC, GPO and DLA orders, and its military signage has shipped worldwide. For bases in Duval, Clay and St. Johns counties, the shop is close enough to visit the site, measure, and install without travel costs eating the budget.

To start a quote, call (904) 272-3395 or email team@brand9signs.com. Brand 9 calls back within 15 minutes during business hours (Mon–Fri, 8:30am–5pm).

## Frequently asked questions

### Can a military base buy a sign with a government purchase card?

Yes, if the total is under the $15,000 micro-purchase threshold (effective October 1, 2025) and the vendor is registered in SAM.gov. Building ID signs and small regulatory sign packages often fall in this range.

### What sign standard do military installations use?

Most DoD installations follow UFC 3-120-01, *Design: Sign Standards*. It sets the sign families, typography, colors and layouts. Many bases add their own facilities or architecture standard on top of it.

### Is there a sign company in Jacksonville registered for federal work?

Yes. Brand 9 Signs in Orange Park, FL is a registered U.S. government contractor (CAGE 0VVG2). It works for GPO and DLA, counts NAVFAC as a client, and fabricates and installs signs with its own crews.

faq.a: Plan blank positions from the start and use a mounting system such as slotted rails, magnetic backers or standoffs on a pre-drilled grid. New plates are made to match the original font, finish and spacing, then slid or snapped into place without new holes in the wall.

faq.q: Do donor walls need to be ADA compliant?
faq.a: Donor walls don't need Braille, but they must follow ADA Section 307 protruding-object limits. Wall-mounted elements with leading edges between 27 and 80 inches above the floor can project no more than 4 inches into the walkway.

items.body_md:
**Short answer:** A donor wall for a college building near Palatka works best when it is planned like a sign system, not a plaque. That means named giving tiers, plates that can be added or swapped without new holes, a wall location that has been checked against the ADA protruding-object rule (4 inches maximum projection between 27 and 80 inches above the floor), and a content owner at the foundation who keeps the list current. Brand 9 Signs, based in Orange Park, designs, fabricates and installs donor recognition signage across Putnam, Clay and St. Johns counties.

## Why donor recognition is a live question in Putnam County

St. Johns River State College opened in Palatka in 1958, and its Palatka campus (the Dr. Robert L. McLendon Jr. Campus on St. Johns Avenue) is still where much of its giving shows up. In September 2025 the college dedicated its new student housing as Beck Hall, honoring the late Carl Beck of Beck Automotive Group, with funding from the Sloan family. Naming gifts like that are the top of the pyramid. Below them sit hundreds of smaller gifts to scholarships, labs and programs, and those donors expect to see their names somewhere too. That is the job of the donor wall.

The same planning applies to hospital foundations, private schools, churches and civic buildings in Palatka, East Palatka and Crescent City.

## What should a college donor wall include?

### Giving tiers people can read from across the lobby

Most walls use three to five tiers, and the tier should be obvious from size and position alone. A common layout puts one or two large plates for leadership or naming gifts at the top, a row of medium plates for major gifts, and a field of small, uniform plates for annual or scholarship donors. Keep the tier names on the wall short (for example "Founders," "Benefactors," "Friends") and put dollar ranges in the foundation's materials, not on the sign.

### Room for names that don't exist yet

The most common mistake we see is a wall that is full on dedication day. Plan 25 to 40 percent of the small-plate field as blank positions, and pick a mounting method that takes new plates without drilling the wall again. Slotted rails, magnetic backers and standoff-mounted plates on a pre-drilled grid all do this. The foundation can then add names after each campaign without hiring a contractor.

### Materials that suit the building

Brushed aluminum and stainless plates suit newer academic buildings. Clear or back-painted acrylic on standoffs reads well in bright lobbies. Etched glass, cast bronze and dimensional letters suit heritage spaces. For any exterior or breezeway location in Florida, use marine-grade (316) stainless hardware and UV-stable inks, because humidity and sun will find the weak point first.

## Does a donor wall have to meet ADA rules?

A donor wall is not a room-identification sign, so it does not need Braille or tactile characters. It does have to follow the ADA's protruding-object rules (2010 ADA Standards, Section 307), because it sits in a circulation path. According to the U.S. Access Board guide:

- Wall-mounted objects with leading edges above 27 inches and below 80 inches can project no more than 4 inches from the wall.
- Free-standing displays on posts or pylons with leading edges in that same range cannot overhang the circulation path by more than 12 inches.
- Anything with its leading edge at 27 inches or lower (within cane sweep), or at 80 inches or higher, can project any amount.

In practice, a standoff-mounted wall with 1- to 2-inch standoffs and thin plates stays well inside the 4-inch limit. A display case, a 3D sculptural element or a digital kiosk needs to be checked before it is ordered.

## How does a donor wall project usually run?

1. **List and tiers (foundation):** confirm tier names, how donors want their names shown, and who approves spelling. Names are the most expensive thing to get wrong.
2. **Wall survey:** measure the wall, check the lighting, and find what is behind the drywall (block, metal stud or blocking). Old buildings on long-established campuses often hide surprises.
3. **Design and proof:** a scaled layout with real names in place, plus the blank positions for future donors.
4. **Fabrication and install:** fabrication normally takes a few weeks after proof approval. Installation in an occupied building is usually one day or less, scheduled around classes or events.
5. **Updates:** a simple spreadsheet of positions so new plates match the original font, finish and spacing years later.

## A local note

Palatka is about an hour south of our Orange Park shop, so survey visits and install days do not need hotel nights or long travel charges. Brand 9 Signs has built recognition, wayfinding and interior signage for Northeast Florida institutions since 1986. If your foundation is planning a dedication, start the wall conversation when the gift is announced, not two weeks before the ribbon cutting.

items.seo_title: Rust Stains on Entrance Signs in Middleburg, FL
items.meta_description: Why Middleburg entrance signs get rust stains from well-water irrigation, how to clean them safely, and design choices that keep new monuments stain-free.

faq.q: What iron level in irrigation water causes rust stains on signs?
faq.a: UF/IFAS reports that staining conditions exist once iron in the water exceeds 0.3 ppm. Florida's limestone aquifers often run at pH 8 or higher. At that pH dissolved iron oxidizes in about 30 seconds, so it settles right where the spray dries on the sign.

faq.q: Will pressure washing remove rust stains from a stucco entrance sign?
faq.a: Usually not on its own, and high pressure can erode the stucco texture and force water behind mounted letters. Use a masonry-safe rust remover, typically oxalic-acid based and tested on a hidden area first, then rinse at low pressure. Redirect the sprinkler first, or the stain will return.

faq.q: Are irrigation rust stains damaging my entrance sign?
faq.a: The iron film itself is cosmetic. It sits on the surface and doesn't weaken the structure. Long-stained porous stucco or natural stone may need a matching recoat to look right again. A streak running from a screw or letter stud is different: it means a steel fastener is corroding and should be replaced with stainless steel.

items.body_md:
**Short answer:** Entrance sign rust stains are almost always an irrigation problem. When a subdivision entrance sign in Middleburg turns rusty brown along the bottom or in a fan shape across its face, the water is to blame. The sign itself is rarely the problem. Florida groundwater carries dissolved iron, and when a sprinkler throws that water onto stucco, stone or painted letters, the iron reacts with air and leaves a reddish film. UF/IFAS puts the threshold low: once iron in the water goes above **0.3 ppm**, staining should be expected. You can clean the stain off, but it comes back until the water stops hitting the sign.

## Why entrance sign rust stains happen in Middleburg

Iron in well water is dissolved (ferrous) iron, and you can't see it. Spraying the water mixes in oxygen, which turns the iron into ferric iron. Ferric iron doesn't dissolve, so it settles onto whatever the spray hits. How fast that happens depends on the water's pH. UF/IFAS figures show the change taking about 100 hours at pH 6.0, about 1 hour at pH 7.0 and about **30 seconds at pH 8.0**. Florida's limestone aquifers often run at pH 8 or higher, so the iron settles almost the moment the water lands. The stain forms where the spray dries: low on the sign face, at the edge of the sprinkler's arc.

This is common around Middleburg. Middleburg is unincorporated Clay County, and many older neighborhoods, acreage lots and HOA common areas water their landscaping from wells rather than utility water.

### How to tell irrigation stains from a failing sign

Where the stain sits tells you what is causing it:

- **A band or fan shape at sprinkler height with a sharp lower edge** is irrigation iron. The sign is fine.
- **A streak running down from a screw, letter stud or cap joint** is hardware rust. A steel fastener is corroding, and it should be replaced with stainless steel.
- **Discoloration only on the letters** points to the letter material or its coating. That is a fabrication issue, not a water one.

## How to clean rust stains off a monument sign

1. **Turn off or redirect the zone first.** Cleaning before the spray is fixed wastes the effort.
2. **Use a rust remover made for masonry**, usually one based on oxalic acid, and test it on a hidden area first. Products made for concrete driveways can be too harsh for painted stucco and for the finish on aluminum or HDU letters.
3. **Rinse at low pressure.** High-pressure washing wears down the stucco texture and can push water behind mounted letters and into the cap joints.
4. **Check the finish once it's dry.** Iron that has sat for years in porous stucco or natural stone may not lift completely. In that case the fix is a recoat in a matching masonry finish, which is still much cheaper than rebuilding.

## Designing a new entrance sign so it doesn't stain

Preventing the stain is cheaper than cleaning it, and almost all of the prevention happens before the landscaping goes in:

- **Keep spray off the sign entirely.** Put the bed directly in front of the monument on drip or bubblers, and set the rotors so their arc stops short of the face. Settle this with the irrigation contractor during site work, not after the first stain appears.
- **Give the sign a darker, sealed base.** A plinth or base course in a darker sealed finish hides the splash zone that every ground-level sign eventually gets.
- **Choose faces that wipe clean.** Powder-coated aluminum and painted HDU faces clean up far more easily than open-texture stucco or porous natural stone.
- **Use stainless steel hardware everywhere.** Letter studs, cap anchors and cabinet fasteners should all be stainless, so the only rust risk is the water, which you can control.
- **Test the well.** If the HOA's irrigation well tests above 0.3 ppm iron, the board can treat the water at the source for every zone rather than chase stains sign by sign.

## Who to call in Middleburg and Clay County

On every entrance sign refurbishment, Brand 9 Signs asks about the irrigation first. We are an Orange Park sign company that has designed, fabricated and installed community entrance monuments since 1986, and in Middleburg the water is often the cause before the sign is. For a new community, we coordinate the monument's finish, base detail and sprinkler layout with the builder and landscaper before anything is poured. That is the stage when preventing stains costs almost nothing.

items.seo_title: Orange Park Sign Permits: Town or Clay County?
items.meta_description: An Orange Park address may not mean a Town permit. Who reviews business signs in Clay County, the 15-day clock, and the limits to plan around.

faq.q: Does an Orange Park address mean I need a Town of Orange Park sign permit?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Only parcels inside the incorporated Town of Orange Park are under the Town's sign rules. Many Orange Park–addressed businesses are in unincorporated Clay County. The parcel record decides it.

faq.q: How long does a sign permit take in unincorporated Clay County?
faq.a: Clay County's Land Development Code requires the sign permit review to be completed within 15 calendar days of the application, with a grant or denial in that window. The building and electrical permits follow. Engineering and complete drawings are usually the longer part of the schedule.

faq.q: What's the tallest freestanding sign allowed in Clay County?
faq.a: Article VII prohibits freestanding signs higher than 40 feet anywhere in unincorporated Clay County. Most monument signs are far shorter. Your actual height and area depend on your zoning district and frontage.

items.body_md:
**Who permits a business sign in Orange Park, Florida?** It depends on the parcel, not the mailing address. Only signs inside the incorporated Town of Orange Park go through the Town. Much of the area that carries an Orange Park address, along Blanding Boulevard and out toward Oakleaf, is unincorporated Clay County. In unincorporated Clay County, the County's Zoning Director (or a designee) reviews the sign permit. Under Article VII of the Clay County Land Development Code, that review "shall be completed within fifteen calendar days." Find out the jurisdiction first. It decides the code, the reviewer and the timeline.

The rest of this guide covers how each step works and which Clay County limits to plan around before anyone designs the sign.

## Step 1: Confirm the jurisdiction (Town of Orange Park or Clay County)

Clay County has four incorporated municipalities: Orange Park, Green Cove Springs, Keystone Heights and Penney Farms. Each writes its own sign rules. Everything outside them is unincorporated Clay County. The County's Land Development Code says it applies to development "located within the unincorporated area of Clay County, Florida."

A five-minute check of the property appraiser's parcel record shows which one you're in. Skip it, and a package drawn to one code may have to be redrawn for the other. The shop in a Kingsley Avenue strip center and the shop on Blanding a few miles south can both say "Orange Park" on their business cards and still be under different codes.

## Step 2: Know what Clay County requires a permit for

Under Article VII (Sign Regulations), a **permanent sign needs a sign permit unless it is specifically exempt** (Sec. 7-12). The application goes to the County Zoning Director or a designee. Review must be completed within **15 calendar days**, and the application is granted or denied within that window (Sec. 7-13). If the work isn't completed within **one year**, the permit becomes **null and void** (Sec. 7-15).

That 15-day clock only starts on a complete application. In practice, the order of a project is:

1. Parcel check and survey or site plan
2. Sign drawings with dimensions, height and area
3. Engineering for structural signs
4. The zoning sign permit
5. The building permit, plus an electrical permit for lit signs, under the Florida Building Code

## Step 3: Clay County sign size, height and setback limits

The County's list of prohibited signs (Sec. 7-5) sets the outer limits. They are worth knowing before you fall in love with a design:

| Limit (unincorporated Clay County) | Value |
|---|---|
| Freestanding sign height | No higher than **40 ft** |
| Freestanding sign area, intensive commercial/industrial districts | Max **500 sq ft** |
| Freestanding sign area, other districts | Max **250 sq ft** |
| Attached (wall) sign area, intensive districts | Max **250 sq ft** |
| Attached (wall) sign area, other districts | Max **125 sq ft** |
| Freestanding sign setback | At least **5 ft** from any property line (Sec. 7-22) |

Those are ceilings, not allowances. The area you're actually allowed is usually smaller, because it's calculated from your street or building frontage and your zoning district. For example, a 60-foot storefront in a neighborhood-commercial district may not get anywhere near the 125 sq ft ceiling. Ask for the frontage calculation before you approve artwork.

### Monument or pole? The code draws the line at 3:1

Clay County defines the difference with a ratio. A **monument sign** has a sign-to-support width ratio of **less than 3 to 1**. At **3 to 1 or more**, it's a **pole sign**. A wide sign face on a narrow pair of posts is a pole sign in the code's eyes, whatever the drawing calls it.

## Step 4: Clay County lighting rules for illuminated signs

Illuminated channel letters and lit monuments are allowed. Two rules matter:

- **No flashing.** Signs that "utilize flashing" are prohibited.
- **Shield the light source.** Signs with "unshielded illuminating devices" are prohibited.

Internally lit letters with LED modules behind acrylic faces meet the shielding rule by design. Exposed bulbs or a raw LED strip around a cabinet edge may not. Every lit sign also needs a dedicated circuit and an electrical permit, so put the electrician on the project from the start.

## A typical timeline for an Orange Park–area business sign

For a typical Blanding Boulevard tenant, the sequence is a parcel check on day one, then drawings and engineering. After that comes the County's 15-day review, followed by building and electrical permits. Fabrication runs in parallel once the drawings are approved, so the bulk of the calendar goes to drawings and engineering rather than the County review itself. Brand 9 Signs has been fabricating and installing commercial signs from Orange Park since 1986. The jurisdiction check is the first thing we do on any Clay County project, because it determines everything that comes after it.

*Code citations are from the Clay County Land Development Code, Article VII (Sign Regulations), as published by the County. Codes are amended. Confirm current limits with Clay County Planning & Zoning, or with the Town of Orange Park for in-town parcels, before you submit.*

items.body_md:
**What does it take to put up a monument sign in Julington Creek?** A monument sign in Julington Creek sits in unincorporated St. Johns County, so it goes through the county, not the City of Jacksonville. The county's Planning & Zoning Division reviews the application, and the Building Services Division issues the building permit once review and fees are complete. Expect to submit a site plan, sign drawings, and, for most masonry or lit monuments, structural calculations sealed by a Florida-registered design professional. The county's sign-permit procedure sets a written decision within 10 days of a *complete* application, and 30 days for signs in an overlay district. An incomplete package is what actually costs weeks.

That is the short answer. Below is what each step requires and how to sequence it so a community entrance or business monument is not stuck waiting on paperwork.

## Julington Creek is St. Johns County, not Jacksonville

Julington Creek straddles the Duval/St. Johns line, and the rules follow the parcel, not the mailing address. A sign on a St. Johns County parcel is permitted under the county's sign-permit procedure (Section 31.0 of the Land Development Code process) and the numeric limits for height, area and setback in the county's Land Development Code. A sign a few hundred yards away on the Duval side is a City of Jacksonville permit with different limits. Confirm the parcel's jurisdiction before anyone draws artwork.

## Who reviews and issues the permit

Planning & Zoning (4040 Lewis Speedway, St. Augustine) reviews the sign application. Building Services issues the building permit after review and payment. Permits go to a licensed sign contractor, or to a property owner acting as their own contractor under Florida law. For an HOA or CDD, that usually means the fabricator pulls the permit as part of the job.

## What the application must show

According to the county's sign-permit procedure, the package includes:

- **A site plan** showing the proposed sign, all setbacks, locations outside any right-of-way, sight triangles, easements, utility lines, road frontage and dimensions to property lines.
- **Sign drawings** showing the height of a ground sign from grade to its highest point, the sign area, and every existing sign on the site.
- **Electrical details** for a lit monument: the fixtures, the disconnect, and a nationally recognized testing lab number for each internally illuminated fixture.
- **Structural details**: foundation cross-section, attachment details and signed, sealed gravity and wind-load calculations from a Florida-registered design professional.

Overlay districts add submittals and a longer review, so check whether the site sits inside one before promising a grand-opening date.

## Where monument signs get delayed

Delays are rarely the sign. They are a site plan with no setback dimensions, a monument drawn into an easement or sight triangle, a lit sign with no testing-lab listing, or footing details that were never engineered for Florida wind loads. Each one sends the application back. A fabricator who has pulled St. Johns County permits will build the package so the first submission is complete.

## A build order that protects the schedule

Confirm jurisdiction and the height and area limits first. Get HOA or developer design approval second, because the county reviews what is built, not what the board prefers. Then submit the permit with engineering attached, fabricate while the review runs, and schedule the footing and install around the permit and the electrician. For price ranges on a community entrance, see our [community entrance sign cost guide for Clay County](/blog/community-entrance-sign-cost-clay-county-fl); the same cost drivers apply across the river.

## Who builds monument signs in Julington Creek

Brand 9 Signs is a sign fabrication and installation company at 1970 Solomon Street in Orange Park, serving Jacksonville, Clay County and St. Johns County since 1986. We fabricate on our own CNC router, handle design, engineering coordination and permitting, and install community and commercial monuments. Whoever you choose, ask for a St. Johns County project reference, a written scope that says who pulls the permit and who pays for engineering, and a quote that separates the sign, footing, lighting and permit fees.

## FAQ

**Does a monument sign in Julington Creek need a permit?**
Signs that require a permit under the Florida Building Code do, and monument signs are covered by the St. Johns County sign-permit application. A Julington Creek parcel in unincorporated St. Johns County is reviewed by the county's Planning & Zoning Division; confirm your parcel's jurisdiction first, since the Duval side is a City of Jacksonville permit.

**How long does a St. Johns County sign permit take?**
The county's procedure calls for a written decision within 10 days of a complete application, and within 30 days for signs in an overlay district. Incomplete applications restart the clock in practice, so a complete first submission matters most.

**Does a lit monument sign need engineering?**
Typically yes. The county asks for structural calculations signed and sealed by a Florida-registered design professional, plus electrical details and a testing-lab number for each internally illuminated fixture.

items.seo_title: Mounting Channel Letters on Stucco in Florida

faq.q: Do I need a permit to install channel letters on my building in Jacksonville?
faq.a: Usually yes. Wall signs, especially illuminated ones, generally require a sign permit and a licensed electrician for the electrical connection. Requirements differ between Jacksonville, Clay County and St. Johns County, so check with the local building department or have your sign company confirm before you order.

faq.q: Can channel letters be mounted on EIFS or synthetic stucco?
faq.a: Yes, but not by anchoring into the foam. Fasteners must reach the structure behind the EIFS, and each penetration needs a careful seal to keep water out of the wall. A raceway mount is often the safer choice because it needs fewer holes.

faq.q: Is raceway or flush mounting better for Florida weather?
faq.a: Neither is automatically better. Flush mount looks cleaner on a wall that can be opened; raceway mount keeps wiring accessible and uses fewer wall penetrations. In either case, what protects the building is stainless or coated fasteners, engineered anchors for wind load, and a sealed penetration at every hole.

items.body_md:
**How are channel letters mounted on a stucco or brick building in Florida?** Two ways. Flush-mount letters are anchored straight into the wall, with the power wiring run through small sealed holes behind each letter. Raceway-mount letters are bolted to a metal channel (the raceway) that carries the wiring, and the raceway is anchored to the wall. Either method needs engineered anchors sized for Florida wind load, a sealed penetration at every fastener, a UL-listed sign, and in most Northeast Florida jurisdictions a permit. The right choice depends on what your wall is made of and how thick the finish is.

Most "my sign leaked" and "my letters shifted" stories trace back to this one step, not to the letters themselves.

## Know your wall before you pick a mount

The finish you can see is not what holds the sign. Ask what is behind it:

- **Stucco over concrete block (CBS):** the most common commercial wall in Jacksonville and Clay County. Anchors go through the stucco into the block or its grout cells. This is a strong substrate when anchored correctly.
- **Stucco over wood or metal framing:** the sign must hit framing or solid blocking. Anchoring into stucco and sheathing alone will not carry the load.
- **EIFS (foam-based "synthetic stucco"):** the foam has almost no holding power. Anchors must reach the structure behind it, and the penetration seal matters even more because water that gets behind EIFS stays there.
- **Brick veneer:** drill through mortar joints where possible, not through the brick face, and anchor to the structure behind the veneer.
- **Metal panel or storefront systems:** need through-bolts or backing plates, and usually input from the building owner or landlord.

A site survey (sometimes with a small test hole) before the sign is built is how a fabricator avoids discovering foam or hollow block on install day.

## Flush mount vs. raceway mount

**Flush mount** gives the cleanest look: letters appear to float on the wall with no visible hardware. It requires access to run wiring inside or behind the wall, or surface conduit that is hidden behind the letters. Best for new construction or walls that can be opened.

**Raceway mount** puts the letters on a painted aluminum channel, typically colored to match the wall. It keeps wiring accessible, requires far fewer wall penetrations, and is the usual answer for existing masonry, EIFS, or any wall where fishing wire is impractical. Many landlords prefer it because removal leaves fewer holes to patch.

If your lease says the wall must be restored when you leave, ask the sign company how many penetrations each option makes.

## Wind load: the Florida part

Signs attached to buildings are designed to the Florida Building Code's wind provisions. For Duval, Clay and St. Johns counties the ultimate design wind speed is generally in the range of 120 to 130 mph depending on location and risk category, and the exact number comes from the engineer, not the sign shop's guess. What that means in practice:

- Anchor diameter, embedment depth and spacing are calculated for the letter height, depth and mounting height.
- Large or tall letters usually need engineered drawings with the permit application.
- Stainless or coated fasteners are standard in this climate. Plain steel in salt-influenced air rusts, and the rust bleeds onto the stucco.

## Seal every hole, every time

Each fastener and wire pass-through is a place for water to enter the wall. A proper install uses a sealant rated for exterior masonry at every penetration, drip-loops the wiring so water runs away from the hole, and keeps electrical connections out of the wet zone. Walls that were stained or bubbled six months after install almost always had a missed seal.

## Electrical and permitting

Illuminated letters should be UL-listed (the sign standard is UL 48) and wired to the National Electrical Code's sign article. In Jacksonville and surrounding counties, an illuminated wall sign typically needs a sign permit and a licensed electrical contractor for the final connection. Permit fees, review times and size limits differ between Jacksonville, Clay County and St. Johns County, and landlords or HOAs may have their own approval step, so confirm those before artwork is final.

## Where Brand 9 Signs fits

Brand 9 Signs has fabricated and installed commercial signage from Orange Park since 1986. For illuminated letters, we survey the wall first, tell you whether it is block, framing or foam, and recommend flush or raceway based on what we find. If you are comparing quotes, ask each company for the same four things in writing: anchor type and material, how penetrations are sealed, UL listing, and who pulls the permit.

## FAQ

**Do I need a permit to install channel letters on my building in Jacksonville?**
Usually yes. Wall signs, especially illuminated ones, generally require a sign permit and a licensed electrician for the electrical connection. Requirements differ between Jacksonville, Clay County and St. Johns County, so check with the local building department or have your sign company confirm before you order.

**Can channel letters be mounted on EIFS or synthetic stucco?**
Yes, but not by anchoring into the foam. Fasteners must reach the structure behind the EIFS, and each penetration needs a careful seal to keep water out of the wall. A raceway mount is often the safer choice because it needs fewer holes.

**Is raceway or flush mounting better for Florida weather?**
Neither is automatically better. Flush mount looks cleaner on a wall that can be opened; raceway mount keeps wiring accessible and uses fewer wall penetrations. In either case, what protects the building is stainless or coated fasteners, engineered anchors for wind load, and a sealed penetration at every hole.

items.body_md:
**How big can a construction sign be in Jacksonville?** The City of Jacksonville allows **one temporary construction sign per construction site**, and the maximum area depends on zoning: **4 square feet** in RR and RLD districts, **16 square feet** in RMD and RHD districts, and **32 square feet** in all other districts. It cannot be placed in City right-of-way. A larger *development identification sign* (up to 100 square feet) is a separate category that needs pre-approval.

That is the question most builders, developers and general contractors in Duval, Clay and St. Johns counties type into a search bar. The rest of this guide covers what the numbers mean in practice.

## Jacksonville construction sign rules at a glance

The City's Building Inspection Division publishes the limits under Chapter 656, Part 13 (Sign Regulations) and Chapter 326 of the Ordinance Code:

- **Count:** one temporary construction sign per site, not one per contractor. If the GC, architect and lender all want billing, they share a single board.
- **Area:** 4 sq ft (RR, RLD), 16 sq ft (RMD, RHD), 32 sq ft (all other districts).
- **Location:** never in City right-of-way. Ground signs generally sit at least 10 ft from any right-of-way or property line and not within 25 ft of a right-of-way intersection.
- **Permit and bond:** a sign permit is required for signs generally, applied for through the City's JAXEPICS portal, typically by a licensed sign contractor. A $5,000 sign bond applies unless the owner applies for a non-illuminated sign of 32 sq ft or less and 8 ft or less in overall height.

Because 32 sq ft is a hard ceiling in commercial zoning, the design question is not "how big?" but "what earns a place on 32 square feet?"

## Construction sign vs. development identification sign

These two get confused, and the difference matters for your schedule.

A **construction sign** says who is building, designing and financing, and who to call. It lives for the length of the job.

A **development identification sign** announces the project itself: "Coming Soon: 124 homes." The City caps it at 100 sq ft, and the application must be pre-approved by the Director of Planning and Development, the City Engineer and the Traffic Engineer. It must also stay inside the area and height limits of its zoning district. Three sign-offs means this is the one to start early.

## What belongs on a 32-square-foot board

On site signs, the usual failure is not size but information overload. A board with six logos, a rendering and a paragraph cannot be read from a passing car.

1. **Project name first.** It must read at road speed. On a 45 mph corridor, size the lettering for several hundred feet of reading distance, then work back to the board.
2. **One call to action.** A leasing line, a sales center address or a contractor phone number, not all three.
3. **Credits in a quiet band.** Architect, GC and lender sit in a lower strip at a fraction of the headline size.
4. **Substrate that survives Florida.** Aluminum or HDPO panels on treated-wood or steel posts hold color and flatness through UV and summer storms better than thin corrugated plastic.

## The other sign on your site

Florida's permit process carries its own on-site requirement. Under Florida Statute 713.135, the building permit warns that a notice of commencement must be recorded and posted on the site before the first inspection. That is a legal notice, not branding, but plan the post location so the two do not collide.

## Who handles this in Northeast Florida

Brand 9 Signs fabricates and installs site signs, development identification boards and community signage from Orange Park in Clay County, and has since 1986. The advice we give every builder is the same: confirm the zoning district first, because that single fact sets your allowed square footage before any design work begins.

*Sign codes change and Clay and St. Johns counties have their own rules. Confirm with the local permitting office before you order.*
